evidence: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:199 tags wait_produce with {'shards': shard_tag}, while :185 (flusher.produce) and :195 (segment_size_bytes) use {'shard': shard_tag}. The inconsistency is real and was added in this PR. But these are different metric names (produce vs wait_produce), not 'the same metric', so no single metric is split. The real cost is that you can't filter or group the sibling flusher metrics with one tag key. One-word fix: use 'shard'.

flusher.py:127-132 defines _create_process_for_shard(shard). grep across src/ and tests/ finds no caller. _ensure_processes_alive (:259) and _create_processes (:84) call _create_process_for_shards directly with the process_index they already know. Dead code; remove it. Routing restarts through it would add a pointless reverse lookup.

flusher.py:35 docstring says 'fowards'. The typo is real but predates this PR (it is at line 33 of the base commit de11fb01, in an unchanged context line). Trivial fix while the docstring is being edited anyway.

flusher.py:254-255. BaseProcess.close() raises ValueError('Cannot close a process while it is still running...') if the child has not been reaped. kill() only sends SIGKILL and returns at once, so calling close() right after kill() without join() would raise. close() also doesn't reap zombies; join()/poll() do, and the next Process.start() (called right away by _create_process_for_shards at :259) runs multiprocessing's _cleanup(), which reaps finished children. The Popen finalizer closes the sentinel fds on GC, and restarts are capped by MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS=10 (:24), so nothing accumulates. Separately, the guarded branch never runs anyway: mp_context.Process is SpawnProcess, whose MRO is (SpawnProcess, BaseProcess, object), so isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) is False (checked in Python) and kill() is never called on a hung process. That is the real bug here (it predates the PR, at base:266) and should be fixed with isinstance(process, multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess) or a not-Thread check.

flusher.py:346-347 in join(). Same problem as #3: terminate() only sends SIGTERM, so close() right after it raises ValueError while the child is still running. This is the shutdown path, the processes are daemon=True (:120), and the consumer process is exiting, so leaked fds or zombies don't matter. As in #3, the isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) check is False for SpawnProcess, so terminate() itself never runs. That is the issue worth fixing, not adding close().

flusher.py:39 documents ':param topic:' but __init__ (:43-49) takes buffer, next_step, max_processes, produce_to_pipe. There is no topic parameter (the topic is resolved inside main() at :159-161). The stale line predates the PR (base:37), but the PR adds the new max_processes parameter without documenting it. Low-cost doc fix.
